chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan and Fadalah from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who forgot the Tawaf of the women (Qada' al-Nisa') until he returned to his family. He said: 'The women are not permissible to him until he visits the House (Kaaba). If he dies, his heir or another person should perform Qada' on his behalf. As for when he is alive, it is not suitable for it to be performed on his behalf. If he forgot the Rami (throwing of pebbles), the two are not equal, for throwing pebbles is a Sunnah and Tawaf is a Fard (obligation).'
And that which indicates that whenever he is unable to return, it is permissible for him to order someone to act as his deputy is what he narrated.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to send women for Qada' al-Nisa' before leaving Mecca?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the missed 'Ziyarat al-Nisa' (visitation of one's family) is a mandatory condition for resuming marital relations, distinguishing its obligatory nature from the Sunnah of Rami. This ruling underscores the practical legal implications of Hajj rituals on personal status, emphasizing that while an heir may perform the visitation on behalf of the deceased, it cannot be substituted while the pilgrim is alive. The hadith highlights the juristic precision in differentiating between Fard (obligatory) and Sunnah acts within the framework of Shia fiqh.
